parameters.name: ContentLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the path of the content. The site system server requires permission to read the content files.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of a deployment type.

parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type uses a custom script to detect the presence of this deployment type.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: ForceForUnknownPublisher
parameters.description: Indicates whether the deployment type requires file signature verification.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specifies the input to this cmdlet. You can use this parameter, or you can pipe the input to this cmdlet.

parameters.name: InstallationBehaviorType
parameters.description: Specifies the installation behavior of the deployment type. Valid values are: * InstallForSystem * InstallForSystemIfResourceIsDeviceOtherwiseInstallForUser * InstallForUser

parameters.name: InstallationProgram
parameters.description: Specifies the command line for the Windows Installer package.

parameters.name: InstallationProgramVisibility
parameters.description: Specifies the mode in which the deployment type runs on client devices. Valid values are: * Normal * Minimized * Maximized * Hidden

parameters.name: InstallationStartIn
parameters.description: Specifies the folder that contains the installation program for the deployment type. This folder can be an absolute path on the client, or a path to the distribution point folder that contains the installation files.

parameters.name: IosInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type detects application information and deployment types from an app package for iOS (.ipa) file.

parameters.name: Language
parameters.description: Specifies an array of languages that the deployment type supports.

parameters.name: LogonRequirementType
parameters.description: Specifies the logon requirement for the deployment type. Valid values are: * OnlyWhenNoUserLoggedOn * OnlyWhenUserLoggedOn * WhereOrNotUserLoggedOn

parameters.name: MacInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type detects application information and deployment types from a Mac OS X Installer (.cmmac) file that was created by using the CMAppUtil tool.

parameters.name: ManualSpecifyDeploymentType
parameters.description: Do not use. Configuration Manager does not currently use this parameter.

parameters.name: MsiInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type detects application information and deployment types from a Windows Installer (.msi) file.

parameters.name: OnFastNetworkMode
parameters.description: Specifies the installation behavior of the deployment type on a fast network. The acceptable values for this parameter are: * RunFromNetwork * RunLocal

parameters.name: OnSlowNetworkMode
parameters.description: Specifies the installation behavior of the deployment type on a slow network. Valid values are: * DoNothing * Download * DownloadContentForStreaming

parameters.name: PersistContentInClientCache
parameters.description: Indicates whether the deployment type saves content in cache indefinitely on the client computer.

parameters.name: PfxFileLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the path of the Personal Information Exchange (PFX) file.

parameters.name: PfxFilePassword
parameters.description: Specifies the password, as a secure string, for the PFX file.

parameters.name: RemoteComputerName
parameters.description: Specifies a remote computer name.

parameters.name: ScriptContent
parameters.description: Specifies the script language that you want to use to detect the deployment type.

parameters.name: ScriptInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type uses a script to detect the presence of this deployment type.

parameters.name: ScriptType
parameters.description: Specifies the script language that you want to use to detect the deployment type.

parameters.name: SignContentFile
parameters.description: Indicates whether the deployment type requires a signed content file.

parameters.name: SignedContentFileLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the path of the signed content file.

parameters.name: WebAppInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that this cmdlet uses a web application installer for the deployment.

parameters.name: WMInstaller

parameters.name: CodeType
parameters.description: Specify the type of return code. This setting defines how Configuration Manager interprets the specified return code from this deployment type. The available types vary based on the deployment type technology. - Failure: The deployment type failed to install. - Success: The deployment type successfully installed, and no reboot is necessary. - FastRetry: Another installation is already in progress on the device. The client retries every two hours, for a total of 10 times. - HardReboot: The deployment type successfully installed, but requires the device to restart. Nothing else can be installed until the device restarts. - SoftReboot: The deployment type successfully installed, but requests the device to restart. Other installations can occur before the device restarts.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Specify an optional description to help you identify and describe this return code.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a deployment type object on which to add the return code. To get this object, use the Get-CMDeploymentType cmdlet.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Specify an optional name to describe this return code.

parameters.name: ReturnCode
parameters.description: Specify an integer value for the return code that you expect from this deployment type. This value is any positive or negative integer between -2147483648 and 2147483647.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf

parameters.name: AddDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses for this deployment type. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then specify those variables as an array for this parameter. For example, -AddDetectionClause $clauseFile1,$clauseFile2,$clauseFile3. You can also use Get-CMDeploymentTypeDetectionClause to get an existing detection clause from another application.

parameters.name: AddLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of language tags that the deployment type supports. For example, to add Russian (Russia), specify the tag ru-RU. For more information and a list of language tags, see Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) Reference.

parameters.name: AddRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement objects for the deployment type. To create a requirement rule object, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMRequirementRuleActiveDirectorySiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleBooleanValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCMSiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCommonValue - New-CMRequirementRuleDeviceOwnershipValue - New-CMRequirementRuleExistential - New-CMRequirementRuleExpression - New-CMRequirementRuleFileAttributeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFilePermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFreeDiskSpaceValue - New-CMRequirementRuleInputTypeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemLanguageValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOUValue - New-CMRequirementRuleRegistryKeyPermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleScreenResolutionValue Starting in version 2111, you can use the Get-CMDeploymentTypeRequirement cmdlet to copy rules from another deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationId
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: CacheContent
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to save content indefinitely in the client cache.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specify an optional description for the deployment type.

parameters.name: ContentFallback
parameters.description: If you set this parameter to $true, when the content isn't available on any distribution points in the client's current or neighbor boundary groups, the client can use distribution points in the site default boundary group.

parameters.name: ContentLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the network source path of the MSI file. The site system server requires permission to read the content files.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeName
parameters.description: Specify a display name for this deployment type.

parameters.name: DetectionClauseConnector
parameters.description: When you use the GroupDetectionClauses parameter to group detection clauses, use this parameter to specify the connector. The following example defines the OR connector: @{"LogicalName"=$clauseFile3.Setting.LogicalName;"Connector"="OR"}

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: EnableBranchCache
parameters.description: This parameter is deprecated. BranchCache is always enabled on clients, and they use it if the distribution point supports it.

parameters.name: EstimatedRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the estimated installation time, in minutes, of this deployment type for the application. Software Center displays this estimate to the user before the application installs.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Forces the command to run without asking for user confirmation.

parameters.name: Force32Bit
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to run the install and uninstall programs as 32-bit processes on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceScriptDetection32Bit
parameters.description: If you use a custom script to detect the presence of this deployment type, set this parameter to $true to run the script as a 32-bit process on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: GroupDetectionClauses
parameters.description: When you configure rules to detect the presence of this deployment type, use this parameter to group clauses. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then use the following format to group clauses: $clause2.Setting.LogicalName, $clause3.Setting.LogicalName. > [!TIP] > In the Configuration Manager console, when you select the Group action, the clauses show parentheses before and after the grouped clauses.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify an application object to configure. To get this object, use the Get-CMApplication cmdlet.

parameters.name: InstallationBehaviorType
parameters.description: Specify the installation behavior for this deployment type: - InstallForUser: The client only installs the application for the user to whom you deploy the application. - InstallForSystem: The client installs the application only once. It's available to all users. - InstallForSystemIfResourceIsDeviceOtherwiseInstallForUser: If you deploy the application to a device, the client installs it for all users. If you deploy the application to a user, the client only installs it for that user.

parameters.name: InstallCommand
parameters.description: Specify the installation program command line to install the Windows Installer package.

parameters.name: InstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the InstallCommand.

parameters.name: LogonRequirementType
parameters.description: Specify the requirement for a signed-in user: - OnlyWhenNoUserLoggedOn: Only when no user is signed into Windows. - OnlyWhenUserLoggedOn: Only when a user is signed in. This option is the default. - WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn: Whether or not a user is signed in. > [!NOTE] > The value WhereOrNotUserLoggedOn is deprecated. It's replaced by WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn. If you set InstallationBehaviorType to InstallForUser, then you can't set this parameter.

parameters.name: MaximumRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the maximum allowed run time of the deployment program for this application. Set an integer value in minutes.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: Specify the MSI product code to set as the detection method. When you use this parameter, it overwrites any other detection methods.

parameters.name: RebootBehavior
parameters.description: Specify the post-installation behavior: - BasedOnExitCode: Determine behavior based on return codes. - NoAction: No specific action. - ProgramReboot: The software install program might force a device restart. - ForceReboot: Configuration Manager client will force a mandatory device restart. For more information on these behaviors, see Create applications in Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: RemoveLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of supported languages to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RemoveRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement rules to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RepairCommand
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command. Also configure the RepairWorkingDirectory parameter. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: RepairWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command's working directory. Also configure the RepairCommand parameter.

parameters.name: RequireUserInteraction
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to allow users to view and interact with the deployment type installation.

parameters.name: ScriptFile
parameters.description: Specify the script file to use to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter.

parameters.name: ScriptLanguage
parameters.description: If you use the ScriptFile or ScriptText parameters, use this parameter to specify the script language.

parameters.name: ScriptText
parameters.description: Specify the text of a script to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter. For more information, see About custom script detection methods.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkDeploymentMode
parameters.description: When a client uses a distribution point from a neighbor boundary group or the default site boundary group, specify the deployment option: - DoNothing: Don't download content - Download: Download content from the distribution point and run locally

parameters.name: SourceUpdateProductCode
parameters.description: Specify an MSI product code. This product code is a GUID format. Windows Source management enables an .MSI represented by this deployment type to automatically be updated or repaired from content source files on an available distribution point.

parameters.name: UninstallCommand
parameters.description: Specifies the command line to uninstall the application. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: UninstallContentLocation
parameters.description: Specify the network path to source content to use with the UninstallCommand that's different from the ContentLocation. Use this parameter when you set UninstallOption to Different.

parameters.name: UninstallOption
parameters.description: Specify what content to use with the UninstallCommand: - SameAsInstall: The install and uninstall content are the same. This option is the default. - NoneRequired: The application doesn't need content for uninstall. - Different: The uninstall content is different from the install content. Use UninstallContentLocation to specify the network path to the content that's used to uninstall the application.

parameters.name: UninstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the UninstallCommand.

parameters.name: UserInteractionMode
parameters.description: Specify the installation program visibility: - Normal: The deployment type runs in the normal mode based on system and program defaults. This mode is the default. - Minimized: The deployment type runs minimized on client devices. Users might see the installation activity in the notification area or taskbar. - Maximized: The deployment type runs maximized on client devices. Users see all installation activity. - Hidden: The deployment type runs hidden on client devices. Users see no installation activity.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

parameters.name: AddDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses for this deployment type. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then specify those variables as an array for this parameter. For example, -AddDetectionClause $clauseFile1,$clauseFile2,$clauseFile3. You can also use Get-CMDeploymentTypeDetectionClause to get an existing detection clause from another application.

parameters.name: AddLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of language tags that the deployment type supports. For example, to add Russian (Russia), specify the tag ru-RU. For more information and a list of language tags, see Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) Reference.

parameters.name: AddRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement objects for the deployment type. To create a requirement rule object, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMRequirementRuleActiveDirectorySiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleBooleanValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCMSiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCommonValue - New-CMRequirementRuleDeviceOwnershipValue - New-CMRequirementRuleExistential - New-CMRequirementRuleExpression - New-CMRequirementRuleFileAttributeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFilePermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFreeDiskSpaceValue - New-CMRequirementRuleInputTypeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemLanguageValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOUValue - New-CMRequirementRuleRegistryKeyPermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleScreenResolutionValue Starting in version 2111, you can use the Get-CMDeploymentTypeRequirement cmdlet to copy rules from another deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationId
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: CacheContent
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to save content indefinitely in the client cache.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specify an optional description for the deployment type.

parameters.name: ContentFallback
parameters.description: If you set this parameter to $true, when the content isn't available on any distribution points in the client's current or neighbor boundary groups, the client can use distribution points in the site default boundary group.

parameters.name: ContentLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the network source path of the content. The site system server requires permission to read the content files.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeName
parameters.description: Specify a display name for this deployment type.

parameters.name: DetectionClauseConnector
parameters.description: When you use the GroupDetectionClauses parameter to group detection clauses, use this parameter to specify the connector. The following example defines the OR connector: @{"LogicalName"=$clauseFile3.Setting.LogicalName;"Connector"="OR"}

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: EnableBranchCache
parameters.description: This parameter is deprecated. BranchCache is always enabled on clients, and they use it if the distribution point supports it.

parameters.name: EstimatedRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the estimated installation time, in minutes, of this deployment type for the application. Software Center displays this estimate to the user before the application installs.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Forces the command to run without asking for user confirmation.

parameters.name: Force32Bit
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to run the install and uninstall programs as 32-bit processes on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceScriptDetection32Bit
parameters.description: If you use a custom script to detect the presence of this deployment type, set this parameter to $true to run the script as a 32-bit process on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: GroupDetectionClauses
parameters.description: When you configure rules to detect the presence of this deployment type, use this parameter to group clauses. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then use the following format to group clauses: $clause2.Setting.LogicalName, $clause3.Setting.LogicalName. > [!TIP] > In the Configuration Manager console, when you select the Group action, the clauses show parentheses before and after the grouped clauses.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify an application object to configure. To get this object, use the Get-CMApplication cmdlet.

parameters.name: InstallationBehaviorType
parameters.description: Specify the installation behavior for this deployment type: - InstallForUser: The client only installs the application for the user to whom you deploy the application. - InstallForSystem: The client installs the application only once. It's available to all users. - InstallForSystemIfResourceIsDeviceOtherwiseInstallForUser: If you deploy the application to a device, the client installs it for all users. If you deploy the application to a user, the client only installs it for that user.

parameters.name: InstallCommand
parameters.description: Specify the installation program command line to install this application.

parameters.name: InstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the InstallCommand.

parameters.name: LogonRequirementType
parameters.description: Specify the requirement for a signed-in user: - OnlyWhenNoUserLoggedOn: Only when no user is signed into Windows. - OnlyWhenUserLoggedOn: Only when a user is signed in. This option is the default. - WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn: Whether or not a user is signed in. > [!NOTE] > The value WhereOrNotUserLoggedOn is deprecated. It's replaced by WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn. If you set InstallationBehaviorType to InstallForUser, then you can't set this parameter.

parameters.name: MaximumRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the maximum allowed run time of the deployment program for this application. Set an integer value in minutes.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: If the application uses Windows Installer technology, specify an MSI product code to set as the detection method. When you use this parameter, it overwrites any other detection methods.

parameters.name: RebootBehavior
parameters.description: Specify the post-installation behavior: - BasedOnExitCode: Determine behavior based on return codes. - NoAction: No specific action. - ProgramReboot: The software install program might force a device restart. - ForceReboot: Configuration Manager client will force a mandatory device restart. For more information on these behaviors, see Create applications in Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: RemoveLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of supported languages to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RemoveRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement rules to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RepairCommand
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command. Also configure the RepairWorkingDirectory parameter. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: RepairWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command's working directory. Also configure the RepairCommand parameter.

parameters.name: RequireUserInteraction
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to allow users to view and interact with the deployment type installation.

parameters.name: ScriptFile
parameters.description: Specify the script file to use to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter.

parameters.name: ScriptLanguage
parameters.description: If you use the ScriptFile or ScriptText parameters, use this parameter to specify the script language.

parameters.name: ScriptText
parameters.description: Specify the text of a script to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter. For more information, see About custom script detection methods.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkDeploymentMode
parameters.description: When a client uses a distribution point from a neighbor boundary group or the default site boundary group, specify the deployment option: - DoNothing: Don't download content - Download: Download content from the distribution point and run locally

parameters.name: SourceUpdateProductCode
parameters.description: If the application uses Windows Installer technology, specify an MSI product code. This product code is a GUID format. Windows Source management enables an .MSI represented by this deployment type to automatically be updated or repaired from content source files on an available distribution point.

parameters.name: UninstallCommand
parameters.description: Specifies the command line to uninstall the application. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: UninstallContentLocation
parameters.description: Specify the network path to source content to use with the UninstallCommand that's different from the ContentLocation. Use this parameter when you set UninstallOption to Different.

parameters.name: UninstallOption
parameters.description: Specify what content to use with the UninstallCommand: - SameAsInstall: The install and uninstall content are the same. This option is the default. - NoneRequired: The application doesn't need content for uninstall. - Different: The uninstall content is different from the install content. Use UninstallContentLocation to specify the network path to the content that's used to uninstall the application.

parameters.name: UninstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the UninstallCommand.

parameters.name: UserInteractionMode
parameters.description: Specify the installation program visibility: - Normal: The deployment type runs in the normal mode based on system and program defaults. This mode is the default. - Minimized: The deployment type runs minimized on client devices. Users might see the installation activity in the notification area or taskbar. - Maximized: The deployment type runs maximized on client devices. Users see all installation activity. - Hidden: The deployment type runs hidden on client devices. Users see no installation activity.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

parameters.name: ImportActionType
parameters.description: Specifies an import action type for the application. If this application already exists in the Software Library, Configuration Manager adds a revision to the existing application unless you modify the action to create a new application. Valid values are: - Skip. This option is not supported. - NotSet. No action is specified. The default behavior is: - If there is a conflict with the application model ID, a new revision is added to the existing application. - If there is a conflict with the application name, a new application is created with a new name. - DirectImport. Imports the application objects. The default behavior is: - If there is a conflict with the application model ID, the error is displayed. - If there is a conflict with the application name, a new application is created with a new name. - Rename. This option is not supported. - Overwrite. Maps objects despite name or scope duplication. If the revision of the application does not match the revision of the application to import, then a new revision is added to the existing application. - ImportFail. This option is not supported.

parameters.description: Specify the type of deadline period. Use this parameter with DeadlineValue.

parameters.name: DeadlineValue
parameters.description: This parameter is only used if you specify AfterPeriod with the InstallationChoice parameter. Specify an integer value for the period of time for the deadline. Use the DeadlineUnit parameter to specify the type of period: Hours, Days, Weeks, Months. This parameter is the same as the following setting on the Settings page of the Create Phased Deployment wizard in the console: Installation is required after this period of time.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Specify a description for the application phased deployment.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: FirstCollection
parameters.description: Specify a collection object for the first phase.

parameters.name: FirstCollectionId
parameters.description: Specify a collection ID for the first phase.

parameters.name: FirstCollectionName
parameters.description: Specify a collection name for the first phase.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior. It's not recommended. You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: InstallationChoice
parameters.description: Specify an option for the behavior relative to when the software is made available: - AsSoonAsPossible: This parameter is the same as the following setting on the Settings page of the Create Phased Deployment wizard in the console: Installation is required as soon as possible. - AfterPeriod: This parameter is the same as the following setting on the Settings page of the Create Phased Deployment wizard in the console: Installation is required after this period of time. If you specify this value, use DeadlineUnit and DeadlineValue to configure the period of time.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Specify a name for the application phased deployment.

parameters.name: SecondCollection
parameters.description: Specify a collection object for the second phase.

parameters.name: SecondCollectionId
parameters.description: Specify a collection ID for the second phase.

parameters.name: SecondCollectionName
parameters.description: Specify a collection name for the second phase.

parameters.name: ThrottlingDays
parameters.description: Specify an integer value for the number of days to gradually make this software available. This parameter is the same as the following setting on the Settings page of the Create Phased Deployment wizard in the console: Gradually make this software available over this period of time (in days).

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

parameters.name: AllowRepairApp
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair application option when creating a deployment for an application.

parameters.name: ApprovalRequired
parameters.description: If you set this parameter to $true, an administrator must approve a request for this application on the device.

parameters.name: AutoCloseExecutable
parameters.description: Starting in version 2107, set this parameter to $true to enable the application deployment setting for install behaviors. Then use the Add-CMDeploymentTypeInstallBehavior cmdlet to add an executable file to check isn't running for the install to succeed. Set this parameter to $false to disable this option in the following situations: - When you use the Remove-CMDeploymentTypeInstallBehavior cmdlet to remove all executable files - You don't want the deployment to check for running executables.

parameters.name: AvailableDateTime
parameters.description: Specify a DateTime object for when this deployment is _available_. To get this object, use the Get-Date built-in cmdlet. Use DeadlineDateTime to specify the deployment assignment, or _deadline_.

parameters.name: Collection
parameters.description: Specify a collection object to which the application is deployed. To get this object, use the Get-CMCollection cmdlet.

parameters.name: CollectionId
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the collection to which this application is deployed. For example, "SMS00004".

parameters.name: CollectionName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the collection to which this application is deployed.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specify an optional comment for this deployment.

parameters.name: DeadlineDateTime
parameters.description: Specify a DateTime object for when this deployment is assigned, also known as the _deadline_. To get this object, use the Get-Date built-in cmdlet. Use -AvailableDateTime to specify when the deployment is _available_.

parameters.name: DeployAction
parameters.description: Specify the deployment action, either to install or uninstall the application. If competing deployments target the same device, the Install action takes priority.

parameters.name: DeployPurpose
parameters.description: Specify the deployment purpose: - Available: The user sees the application in Software Center. They can install it on demand. - Required: The client automatically installs the app according to the schedule that you set. If the application isn't hidden, a user can track its deployment status. They can also use Software Center to install the application before the deadline.

parameters.name: DisableContentDependencyDetection
parameters.description: Add this parameter to not automatically distribute content for dependent apps.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: DistributeCollectionName
parameters.description: The site distributes content to the distribution points that are associated with this collection name.

parameters.name: DistributeContent
parameters.description: Add this parameter if you need to distribute the app content first.

parameters.name: DistributionPointGroupName
parameters.description: To distribute the application content, specify the name of a distribution point group.

parameters.name: DistributionPointName
parameters.description: To distribute the application content, specify the name of a distribution point.

parameters.name: EnableMomAlert
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to enable System Center Operations Manager maintenance mode for this deployment.

parameters.name: EnableSoftDeadline
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to enable delayed enforcement.

parameters.name: FailParameterValue
parameters.description: Specifies the percentage of failed application installation that causes an alert. Specify an integer from 1 through 100. To enable this alert, set the CreatAlertBaseOnPercentFailure parameter to $True.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: GenerateScomAlertOnFailure
parameters.description: Indicates whether to create an Operations Manager alert if a client fails to install the application.

parameters.name: Id
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the application to deploy.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify an application object to deploy. To get this object, use the Get-CMApplication cmdlet.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Specify the name of the application to deploy.

parameters.name: OverrideServiceWindow
parameters.description: Indicates whether the deployment takes place even if scheduled outside of a maintenance window. A maintenance window is a specified period of time used for computer maintenance and updates. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager deploys the application even if the scheduled time falls outside the maintenance window. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager doesn't deploy the application outside the window. It waits until it can deploy in an available window.

parameters.name: PersistOnWriteFilterDevice
parameters.description: Indicates whether to enable write filters for embedded devices. For a value of $True, the device commits changes during a maintenance window. This action requires a restart. For a value of $False, the device saves changes in an overlay and commits them later.

parameters.name: PostponeDateTime
parameters.description: When you set CreateAlertBaseOnPercentSuccess to $true, use this parameter to specify a DateTime object. Configuration Manager creates a deployment alert when the threshold is lower than the SuccessParameterValue after this date. To get this object, use the Get-Date built-in cmdlet.

parameters.name: PreDeploy
parameters.description: Indicates whether to pre-deploy the application to the primary device of the user.

parameters.name: RebootOutsideServiceWindow
parameters.description: Indicates whether a computer restarts outside a maintenance window. A maintenance window is a specified period of time used for computer maintenance and updates. If this value is $True, any required restart takes place without regard to maintenance windows. If this value is $False, the computer doesn't restart outside a maintenance window.

parameters.name: ReplaceToastNotificationWithDialog
parameters.description: When required software is available on the client, set this parameter to $true to replace the default toast notifications with a dialog window. It's false by default. For more information, see Replace toast notifications with dialog window.

parameters.name: SendWakeupPacket
parameters.description: Indicates whether to send a wake-up packet to computers before the deployment begins. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager attempts to wake a computer from sleep. If this value is $False, it doesn't wake computers from sleep. For computers to wake, you must first configure Wake On LAN.

parameters.name: Simulation
parameters.description: Add this parameter to create a deployment simulation. For more information, see Simulate application deployments with Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: SuccessParameterValue
parameters.description: Specifies the percentage of successful application installation that causes an alert. Specify an integer from 0 through 99. To enable this alert, set the CreateAlertBaseOnPercentSuccess parameter as $True.

parameters.name: TimeBaseOn
parameters.description: Specifies which time zone to use: - LocalTime: Use local time. - UTC: Use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

parameters.name: UpdateSupersedence
parameters.description: For an available deployment, use this parameter to specify the installation deadline to upgrade users or devices that have the superseded application installed. Use DeadlineDateTime to specify a specific time, otherwise it's as soon as possible after the AvailableDateTime.

parameters.name: UseMeteredNetwork
parameters.description: Indicates whether to allow clients to download content over a metered internet connection after the deadline, which may incur extra expense.

parameters.name: UserNotification
parameters.description: Specifies the type of user notification. - DisplayAll: Display in Software Center and show all notifications. - DisplaySoftwareCenterOnly: Display in Software Center, and only show notifications of computer restarts. - HideAll: Hide in Software Center and all notifications.

parameters.name: AllowFallback
parameters.description: Allow clients to use distribution points from the default site boundary group.

parameters.name: AllowSharedContent
parameters.description: Allow clients to use distribution points from a neighbor boundary group.

parameters.name: AvailableDateTime
parameters.description: Specify when this deployment is _available_. Use -DeadlineDateTime to specify when the deployment _expires_, and -Schedule to specify the deployment assignment, or _deadline_. To get a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: Collection
parameters.description: Specify a collection object as the target for this package deployment. To get this object, use the Get-CMCollection cmdlet.

parameters.name: CollectionId
parameters.description: Specify a collection ID as the target for this package deployment.

parameters.name: CollectionName
parameters.description: Specify a collection name as the target for this package deployment.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specify an optional comment for this package deployment.

parameters.name: DeadlineDateTime
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify when the deployment _expires_. Use -AvailableDateTime to specify when the deployment is _available_, and -Schedule to specify the deployment assignment, or _deadline_. To get a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeployPurpose
parameters.description: Specify whether this deployment is available for users to install, or it's required to install at the deadline.

parameters.name: DeviceProgram
parameters.description: If the program for the package that you're deploying is a device-type program, specify this parameter. Otherwise, use the StandardProgram parameter. The standard program type is for computers with the Configuration Manager client.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: DistributeCollectionName
parameters.description: The site distributes content to the distribution point groups that are associated with this collection name.

parameters.name: DistributeContent
parameters.description: Add this parameter to distribute the package content when you create this deployment. Clients can't install the package until you distribute content to distribution points that the clients can access.

parameters.name: DistributionPointGroupName
parameters.description: The site distributes content to this distribution point group.

parameters.name: DistributionPointName
parameters.description: The site distributes content to this distribution point.

parameters.name: FastNetworkOption
parameters.description: Specify the behavior when the client uses a distribution point from the current boundary group: - Run program from distribution point - Download content from distribution point and run locally If you don't specify this parameter, it uses DownloadContentFromDistributionPointAndRunLocally by default. This option is more secure, because the client validates the content hash before it runs the program.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: Package
parameters.description: Specify a package object with the program to deploy. To get this object, use the Get-CMPackage cmdlet.

parameters.name: PackageId
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the package with the program to deploy. This ID is a standard package ID, for example XYZ007E3.

parameters.name: PackageName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the package with the program to deploy.

parameters.name: PersistOnWriteFilterDevice
parameters.description: Configure how the client handles the write filter on Windows Embedded devices. - $true: Commit changes at the deadline or during a maintenance window. A restart is required. - $false: Apply content on the overlay and commit later.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: Specify a program object to deploy. To get this object, use the Get-CMProgram cmdlet.

parameters.name: ProgramName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the program in the package to deploy.

parameters.name: RecurUnit
parameters.description: Specify a unit for a recurring deployment. Use the RecurValue parameter to specify the value for this unit.

parameters.name: RecurValue
parameters.description: Specify how often the deployment recurs. This parameter depends on the unit type specified in the RecurUnit parameter: - Hours: This value can be between 1 and 23 - Days: Between 1 and 31 - Minutes: Between 1 and 59

parameters.name: Rerun
parameters.description: Indicate whether the deployment reruns: - $True: The deployment runs again for clients as specified in the RerunBehavior parameter. This value is the default. - $False: The deployment doesn't run again.

parameters.name: RerunBehavior
parameters.description: Specify whether the program reruns on a computer. - NeverRerunDeployedProgram: Doesn't rerun, even if the deployment failed or files changed. - AlwaysRerunProgram: Rerun as scheduled, even if the deployment succeeded. You can use this value for recurring deployments. This value is the default. - RerunIfFailedPreviousAttempt: Rerun as scheduled, if the deployment failed on the previous attempt. - RerunIfSucceededOnPreviousAttempt: Rerun only if the previous attempt succeeded.

parameters.name: RunFromSoftwareCenter
parameters.description: Allow users to run the program independently of assignments.

parameters.name: Schedule
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the deployment assignment, or _deadline_. Use -AvailableDateTime to specify when the deployment is _available_, and -DeadlineDateTime to specify when the deployment _expires_. Specify an array of schedule objects. A schedule object defines the mandatory assignment schedule for a deployment. To create a schedule object, use the New-CMSchedule cmdlet.

parameters.name: ScheduleEvent
parameters.description: Specify the event type that determines when the package deployment runs.

parameters.name: SendWakeupPacket
parameters.description: Indicates whether to send a wake-up packet to computers before the deployment begins. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager wakes a computer from sleep. If this value is $False, it doesn't wake computers from sleep. For computers to wake, first configure Wake On LAN.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkOption
parameters.description: Specify the behavior when the client uses a distribution point from a neighbor boundary group or the default site boundary group: - Do not run program - Download content from distribution point and run locally - Run program from distribution point If you don't specify this parameter, it uses DoNotRunProgram by default.

parameters.name: SoftwareInstallation
parameters.description: When the installation deadline is reached, set this parameter to $true to allow the package to install outside the maintenance window.

parameters.name: StandardProgram
parameters.description: Use this parameter for standard program types. This type is for computers with the Configuration Manager client. If the program for the package that you're deploying is a device-type program, use the DeviceProgram parameter.

parameters.name: SystemRestart
parameters.description: When the installation deadline is reached, set this parameter to $true to allow system restart if necessary outside the maintenance window.

parameters.name: UseMeteredNetwork
parameters.description: Indicates whether to allow clients on a metered internet connection to download content after the installation deadline, which might incur more cost.

parameters.name: UseUtc
parameters.description: Indicates whether clients use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to determine the availability of a program. UTC time makes the deployment available at the same time for all computers. If you don't specify this parameter, or set it to $false, the client uses its local time.

parameters.name: UseUtcForAvailableSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether clients use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to determine the availability of a program. UTC time makes the deployment available at the same time for all computers. If you don't specify this parameter, or set it to $false, the client uses its local time.

parameters.name: UseUtcForExpireSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether clients use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to determine when a program is expired. UTC time expires the deployment at the same time for all computers. If you don't specify this parameter, or set it to $false, the client uses its local time.

Using double quotation marks (") may cause the task sequence step to incorrectly process the parameter. For example: -Arg1 '%TSVar1%' -Arg2 '%TSVar2%' You can also set this parameter to a task sequence variable. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager deploys the application even if the scheduled time falls outside the maintenance window. parameters.name: AddRequirement
parameters.description: Adds an array of requirements for this deployment type.

parameters.name: AdministratorComment
parameters.description: Specifies a description for the deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of the deployment application that contains the deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationNameInWindowsStore
parameters.description: Specifies the name of the application in the Windows Store.

parameters.name: AppV5xInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type detects application information and deployment types from a Application Virtualization (App-V) 5.0 .appv package file.

parameters.name: AppVInstaller
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type detects application information and deployment types from an App-V .appv package file.

parameters.name: ClearRequirements
parameters.description: Indicates that this cmdlet clears the deployment type requirements.

parameters.name: ContentLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the path of the content. The site system server requires permission to read the content files.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeId
parameters.description: Specifies the type ID for a deployment type.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of a deployment type.

parameters.name: DetectDeploymentTypeByCustomScript
parameters.description: Indicates that the deployment type uses a custom script to detect the presence of this deployment type.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: EnableBranchCache
parameters.description: Indicates that clients that use Windows BranchCache are allowed to download content from an on-premises distribution point. Content downloads from cloud-based distribution points can always be shared by clients that use Windows BranchCache.

parameters.name: EnableContentLocationFallback
parameters.description: Indicate whether allows clients to use fall back source location for the content.

parameters.name: EnablePeerToPeerContentDistribution
parameters.description: Indicates whether clients can distribute content to other clients.

parameters.name: EnableUserUninstall

parameters.name: CodeType
parameters.description: Specify the type of return code. This setting defines how Configuration Manager interprets the specified return code from this deployment type. The available types vary based on the deployment type technology. - Failure: The deployment type failed to install. - Success: The deployment type successfully installed, and no reboot is necessary. - FastRetry: Another installation is already in progress on the device. The client retries every two hours, for a total of 10 times. - HardReboot: The deployment type successfully installed, but requires the device to restart. Nothing else can be installed until the device restarts. - SoftReboot: The deployment type successfully installed, but requests the device to restart. Other installations can occur before the device restarts.

parameters.description: Add this parameter to return an object that represents the item with which you're working. By default, this cmdlet may not generate any output.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: Specify the MSI product code to set as the detection method. When you use this parameter, it overwrites any other detection methods.

parameters.name: RebootBehavior
parameters.description: Specify the post-installation behavior: - BasedOnExitCode: Determine behavior based on return codes. - NoAction: No specific action. - ProgramReboot: The software install program might force a device restart. - ForceReboot: Configuration Manager client will force a mandatory device restart. For more information on these behaviors, see Create applications in Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: RemoveDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses to remove.

parameters.name: RemoveLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of supported languages to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RemoveRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement rules to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RepairCommand
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command. Also configure the RepairWorkingDirectory parameter. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: RepairWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command's working directory. Also configure the RepairCommand parameter.

parameters.name: RequireUserInteraction
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to allow users to view and interact with the deployment type installation.

parameters.name: ScriptFile
parameters.description: Specify the script file to use to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter.

parameters.name: ScriptLanguage
parameters.description: If you use the ScriptFile or ScriptText parameters, use this parameter to specify the script language.

parameters.name: ScriptText
parameters.description: Specify the text of a script to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter. For more information, see About custom script detection methods.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkDeploymentMode
parameters.description: When a client uses a distribution point from a neighbor boundary group or the default site boundary group, specify the deployment option: - DoNothing: Don't download content - Download: Download content from the distribution point and run locally

parameters.name: SourceUpdateProductCode
parameters.description: Specify an MSI product code. This product code is a GUID format. Windows Source management enables an .MSI represented by this deployment type to automatically be updated or repaired from content source files on an available distribution point.

parameters.name: UninstallCommand
parameters.description: Specifies the command line to uninstall the application. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: UninstallContentLocation
parameters.description: Specify the network path to source content to use with the UninstallCommand that's different from the ContentLocation. Use this parameter when you set UninstallOption to Different.

parameters.name: UninstallOption
parameters.description: Specify what content to use with the UninstallCommand: - SameAsInstall: The install and uninstall content are the same. This option is the default. - NoneRequired: The application doesn't need content for uninstall. - Different: The uninstall content is different from the install content. Use UninstallContentLocation to specify the network path to the content that's used to uninstall the application.

parameters.name: UninstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the UninstallCommand.

parameters.name: UserInteractionMode
parameters.description: Specify the installation program visibility: - Normal: The deployment type runs in the normal mode based on system and program defaults. This mode is the default. - Minimized: The deployment type runs minimized on client devices. Users might see the installation activity in the notification area or taskbar. - Maximized: The deployment type runs maximized on client devices. Users see all installation activity. - Hidden: The deployment type runs hidden on client devices. Users see no installation activity.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

examples: Set-CMPackage -Id "ST120001" -NewName "ScriptsPackage02" -Description "This package deploys scripts that run on a recurring schedule."

parameters.name: CopyToPackageShareOnDistributionPoint
parameters.description: Clients can always download a package from a distribution point. If you set this parameter to $true, the site makes it available via a named network share on distribution points. Use CustomPackageShareName to specify a custom share name. When you enable this option, more space is required on distribution points. It applies to all distribution points to which you distribute this package.

parameters.name: CustomPackageShareName
parameters.description: If you enable CopyToPackageShareOnDistributionPoint, you can use this parameter to customize the share name. The maximum length is 127 characters, and can't include any of the following characters: " / [ ] : | < > + = ; , ? *. You can specify a share name and a folder name, but then the maximum for each is 80 characters. For example, ShareName\FolderName.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Specify an optional description of the package to help you identify it. You can use a maximum of 128 characters.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: DisconnectUserFromDistributionPoint
parameters.description: This option is deprecated. It sets the ForcedDisconnectEnabled property of the driver package.

parameters.name: DisconnectUserFromDistributionPointMins
parameters.description: This option is deprecated. It sets the ForcedDisconnectDelay property of the driver package.

parameters.name: DisconnectUserFromDistributionPointRetry
parameters.description: This option is deprecated. It sets the ForcedDisconnectNumRetries property of the driver package.

parameters.name: DistributionPointUpdateSchedule
parameters.description: Use this parameter to update distribution points on a schedule. To get a schedule object, use the New-CMSchedule cmdlet.

parameters.name: EnableBinaryDeltaReplication
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to enable binary differential replication (BDR). For more information, see Fundamental concepts for content management in Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: Id
parameters.description: Specify the ID of a package to configure. This value is a standard package ID, for example: XYZ00020.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a package object to configure. To get this object, use the Get-CMPackage cmdlet.

parameters.name: Language
parameters.description: Specify a language string for the package. You can use a maximum of 32 characters in a format that you choose to use to identify the language version. To identify a package, Configuration Manager uses the Language, Manufacturer, Name, and Version parameters. For example, you can have an English version and a German version of the same package.

parameters.name: Manufacturer
parameters.description: Specify the manufacturer name for the software. You can use a maximum of 32 characters. To identify a package, Configuration Manager uses the Language, Manufacturer, Name, and Version parameters.

parameters.name: MifFileName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the Management Information Format (MIF) file that contains the package status. The file name extension must be .mif. Use a status MIF file to generate detailed status reporting. To generate a status MIF file, your application must call the InstallStatusMIF function. For more information, see Status MIF Functions. If you set this parameter, when the client runs the deployment, the Configuration Manager client looks in the %TEMP% directory or the %windir% directory for the installation status MIF file that you specify. The installation status indicates whether the program successfully ran. If the client doesn't find the file, it searches for all MIF files in those directories. It makes a case-insensitive comparison of the values that you specify for MifName, MifPublisher, and MifVersion to the values that the MIF file specifies. If the client finds a match, it uses the status that the MIF file specifies as the installation status for the program. If it can't find a match, or if you don't specify MifFileName, the client uses the program exit code to set the installation status for the program. An exit code of zero indicates that the program successfully ran. Any other values indicate application-specific error codes.

parameters.name: MifName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the package for MIF matching, up to 50 characters. For more information, see the MifFileName parameter.

parameters.name: MifPublisher
parameters.description: Specify the software publisher of the package for MIF matching, up to 32 characters. For more information, see the MifFileName parameter.

parameters.name: MifVersion
parameters.description: Specify the version number of the package for MIF matching, up to 32 characters. For more information, see the MifFileName parameter.

parameters.name: MulticastAllow
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to allow this package to be transferred via multicast. For more information, see Use multicast to deploy Windows over the network with Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: MulticastEncrypt
parameters.description: If you enable MulticastAllow, set this parameter to $true to encrypt multicast packages.

parameters.name: MulticastTransferOnly
parameters.description: If you enable MulticastAllow, set this parameter to $true to only transfer this driver package via multicast.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Specify a package name. You can use a maximum of 250 characters. To identify a package, Configuration Manager uses the Language, Manufacturer, Name, and Version parameters.

parameters.name: NewName
parameters.description: Use this parameter to rename a package.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Add this parameter to return an object that represents the item with which you're working. By default, this cmdlet may not generate any output.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: If the package contains source files, specify the location of the files. You can specify either a full local path on the site server, or a network path. Make sure that this location contains all the files and subdirectories that the program needs to run, including any scripts.

parameters.name: PersistContentInCache
parameters.description: If you don't want the content of this package to age out of the client cache to make room for other content, set this parameter to $true to persist it in the client cache.

parameters.name: PrestageBehavior
parameters.description: Specify the behavior when you enable a distribution point for prestaged content: - ManualCopy: Manually copy the content in this package to the distribution point - DownloadDelta: Download only content changes to the distribution point - OnDemand: Automatically download content when packages are assigned to distribution points For more information, see Use prestaged content.

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: Specify the order in which the site sends the content to other sites and the distribution points in this site. The site sends high priority content before packages with normal or low priority. Packages with equal priority are sent in the order in which they're created.

parameters.name: SendToPreferredDistributionPoint
parameters.description: If you want to enable on-demand content distribution to preferred distribution points, set this parameter to $true. When you enable this setting, if a client requests the content for the package and the content isn't available on any distribution points, then the management point distributes the content. For more information, see On-demand content distribution.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.description: Specify a version number for the software. The maximum length of this string is 32 characters. To identify a package, Configuration Manager uses the Language, Manufacturer, Name, and Version parameters.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Add this parameter to prompt for confirmation before the cmdlet runs.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.
