parameters.name: AllowFallback
parameters.description: {{ Fill AllowFallback Description }}

parameters.name: AllowSharedContent
parameters.description: Indicates whether clients use shared content. If this value is $True, clients attempt to download content from other clients that downloaded that content. If this value is $False, clients do not attempt to download from other clients.

parameters.name: Collection
parameters.description: Specifies the user collection.

parameters.name: CollectionId
parameters.description: Specifies the ID of a device or user collection.

parameters.name: CollectionName
parameters.description: Specifies the ID of a device or user collection.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specifies a comment for the deployment.

parameters.name: DeploymentAvailableDateTime
parameters.description: Specifies, as a DateTime object, the date and time that the deployment becomes available. To obtain a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeploymentExpireDateTime
parameters.description: Specifies, as a DateTime object, the date and time that the deployment expires. To obtain a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeploymentStartDateTime
parameters.description: Specifies, as a DateTime object, the date and time that the deployment starts. To obtain a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeviceProgramName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of a device program.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: EnableExpireSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether to enable the schedule to expire the deployment.

parameters.name: FastNetworkOption
parameters.description: Specifies client behavior on a fast network. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - DownloadContentFromDistributionPointAndRunLocally - RunProgramFromDistributionPoint

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specifies a package object.

parameters.name: PackageId
parameters.description: Specifies the ID of a package.

parameters.name: PackageName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of a package.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Returns the current working object. By default, this cmdlet does not generate any output.

parameters.name: PersistOnWriteFilterDevice
parameters.description: Indicates whether to enable write filters for embedded devices. For a value of $True, the device commits changes during a maintenance window. This action requires a restart. For a value of $False, the device saves changes in an overlay and commits them later.

parameters.name: RecurUnit
parameters.description: Specifies a unit for a recurring deployment. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - Days - Hours - Minutes

parameters.name: RecurValue
parameters.description: Specifies how often a deployment recurs. This parameter depends on the unit type specified in the *RecurUnit* parameter. This value can be between 1 and 23 if the unit is Hours, between 1 and 31 if the unit is Days, or between 1 and 59 if the unit is Minutes.

parameters.name: Rerun
parameters.description: Indicates whether the deployment reruns. If this value is $True, the deployment runs again for clients as specified in the *RerunBehavior* parameter. If this value is $False, the deployment does not run again.

parameters.name: RerunBehavior
parameters.description: Specifies how a deployment reruns on a client. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - AlwaysRerunProgram. Rerun as scheduled, even if the deployment succeeded. You can use this value for recurring deployments. - NeverRerunDeployedProgram. Does not rerun, even if the deployment failed or files changed. - RerunIfFailedPreviousAttempt. Rerun, as scheduled, if the deployment failed on the previous attempt. - RerunIfSucceededOnpreviousAttempt. Rerun only if the previous attempt succeeded. You can use this value for updates that depend on the previous update.

parameters.name: RunFromSoftwareCenter
parameters.description: Indicates whether to run from software center.

parameters.name: Schedule
parameters.description: Specifies a CMSchedule object. The schedule specifies when the maintenance window occurs. To create a CMSchedule object, use the New-CMSchedule cmdlet.

parameters.name: ScheduleEvent
parameters.description: Specifies an array of schedule event types. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - AsSoonAsPossible - LogOff - LogOn - SendWakeUpPacket

parameters.name: SendWakeupPacket
parameters.description: Indicates whether to send a wake-up packet to computers before the deployment begins. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager wakes a computer from sleep. If this value is $False, it does not wake computers from sleep. For computers to wake, you must first configure Wake On LAN.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkOption
parameters.description: Specifies how Configuration Manager deploys this package in a slow network. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - DoNotRunProgram - DownloadContentFromDistributionPointAndLocally - RunProgramFromDistributionPoint

parameters.name: SoftwareInstallation
parameters.description: Indicates whether to install the deployed software outside of maintenance windows. A maintenance window is a specified period of time used for computer maintenance and updates. If this value is $True, the Configuration Manager installs software according to schedule, even if the schedule falls outside a maintenance window. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager does not install deployed software outside any windows, but waits for a maintenance window.

parameters.name: StandardProgramName
parameters.description: Specifies a standard program name.

parameters.name: SystemRestart
parameters.description: Indicates whether a system restarts outside a maintenance window. A maintenance window is a specified period of time used for computer maintenance and updates. If this value is $True, any required restart takes place without regard to maintenance windows. If this value is $False, the computer does not restart outside a maintenance window.

parameters.name: UseMeteredNetwork
parameters.description: {{ Fill UseMeteredNetwork Description }}

parameters.name: UseRecurrencePattern
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use a recurrence pattern.

parameters.name: UseUtc
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), also known as Greenwich Mean Time. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager uses UTC for this deployment. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager uses local time.

parameters.name: UseUtcForAvailableSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use UTC for available schedule. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager uses UTC. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager uses local time.

parameters.name: UseUtcForExpireSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use UTC for expire schedule. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager uses UTC. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager uses local time.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior. It's not recommended. You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a script object to modify. To get this object, use the Get-CMScript cmdlet.

parameters.name: ScriptFile
parameters.description: Specify the network path to a PowerShell script to import and use for this script.

parameters.name: ScriptGuid
parameters.description: Specify the GUID for the script to modify.

parameters.name: ScriptName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the script to modify.

parameters.name: ScriptText
parameters.description: Specify the text to use for this script.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

examples:
$clauseFile1 = New-CMDetectionClauseFile -FileName "abc" -Path "c:\abc" -PropertyType Size -ExpectedValue 1024 -ExpressionOperator IsEquals -Value
$clauseFile2 = New-CMDetectionClauseFile -FileName "abc" -Path "c:\abc" -PropertyType Size -ExpectedValue 2048 -ExpressionOperator IsEquals -Value
$clauseFile3 = New-CMDetectionClauseFile -FileName "abc" -Path "c:\abc" -PropertyType Size -ExpectedValue 4096 -ExpressionOperator IsEquals -Value

Set-CMScriptDeploymentType -ApplicationName "testApp1" -DeploymentTypeName "abc" -AddDetectionClause $clauseFile1,$clauseFile2,$clauseFile3 -DetectionClauseConnector @{"LogicalName"=$clauseFile3.Setting.LogicalName;"Connector"="OR"} -GroupDetectionClauses $clauseFile2.Setting.LogicalName, $clauseFile3.Setting.LogicalName

$myGC = Get-CMGlobalCondition -Name "Operating System Language" | Where-Object PlatformType -eq 1
$cultureA = [System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::GetCultures([System.Globalization.CultureTypes]::AllCultures) | Where-Object Name -eq "zh"
$cultureB = [System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::GetCultures([System.Globalization.CultureTypes]::AllCultures) | Where-Object Name -eq "zh-CN"
$myRule = $myGC | New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemLanguageValue -RuleOperator NoneOf -Culture $cultureA,$cultureB -IsMobile $False

Set-CMScriptDeploymentType -ApplicationName "myApp" -DeploymentTypeName "myDT" -AddRequirement $myRule

$rule1 = Get-CMGlobalCondition -Name "Total physical memory" | New-CMRequirementRuleCommonValue -Value1 2048 -RuleOperator GreaterEquals
$myRuleExpression = New-CMRequirementRuleExpression -AddRequirementRule $rule1
$myGC = New-CMGlobalConditionExpression -Name "GCExp" -DeviceType Windows -RootExpression $myRuleExpression

Set-CMScriptDeploymentType -ApplicationName "myApp" -DeploymentTypeName "myDT" -AddRequirement $myGC

parameters.name: AddDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses for this deployment type. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then specify those variables as an array for this parameter. For example, -AddDetectionClause $clauseFile1,$clauseFile2,$clauseFile3. You can also use Get-CMDeploymentTypeDetectionClause to get an existing detection clause from another application.

parameters.name: AddLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of language tags that the deployment type supports. For example, to add Russian (Russia), specify the tag ru-RU. For more information and a list of language tags, see Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) Reference.

parameters.name: AddRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement objects for the deployment type. To create a requirement rule object, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMRequirementRuleActiveDirectorySiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleBooleanValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCMSiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCommonValue - New-CMRequirementRuleDeviceOwnershipValue - New-CMRequirementRuleExistential - New-CMRequirementRuleExpression - New-CMRequirementRuleFileAttributeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFilePermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFreeDiskSpaceValue - New-CMRequirementRuleInputTypeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemLanguageValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOUValue - New-CMRequirementRuleRegistryKeyPermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleScreenResolutionValue Starting in version 2111, you can use the Get-CMDeploymentTypeRequirement cmdlet to copy rules from another deployment type.

parameters.name: Application
parameters.description: Specify an application object for this deployment type. To get this object, use the Get-CMApplication cmdlet.

parameters.name: ApplicationId
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: CacheContent
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to save content indefinitely in the client cache.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specify an optional description for the deployment type.

parameters.name: ContentFallback
parameters.description: If you set this parameter to $true, when the content isn't available on any distribution points in the client's current or neighbor boundary groups, the client can use distribution points in the site default boundary group.

parameters.name: ContentLocation
parameters.description: Specifies the network source path of the content. The site system server requires permission to read the content files.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the deployment type to configure.

parameters.name: DetectionClauseConnector
parameters.description: When you use the GroupDetectionClauses parameter to group detection clauses, use this parameter to specify the connector. The following example defines the OR connector: @{"LogicalName"=$clauseFile3.Setting.LogicalName;"Connector"="OR"}

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: EnableBranchCache
parameters.description: This parameter is deprecated. BranchCache is always enabled on clients, and they use it if the distribution point supports it.

parameters.name: EstimatedRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the estimated installation time, in minutes, of this deployment type for the application. Software Center displays this estimate to the user before the application installs.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Forces the command to run without asking for user confirmation.

parameters.name: Force32Bit
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to run the install and uninstall programs as 32-bit processes on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceScriptDetection32Bit
parameters.description: If you use a custom script to detect the presence of this deployment type, set this parameter to $true to run the script as a 32-bit process on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: GroupDetectionClauses
parameters.description: When you configure rules to detect the presence of this deployment type, use this parameter to group clauses. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then use the following format to group clauses: $clause2.Setting.LogicalName, $clause3.Setting.LogicalName. > [!TIP] > In the Configuration Manager console, when you select the Group action, the clauses show parentheses before and after the grouped clauses.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a deployment type object to configure. To get this object, use the Get-CMDeploymentType cmdlet.

parameters.name: InstallationBehaviorType
parameters.description: Specify the installation behavior for this deployment type: - InstallForUser: The client only installs the application for the user to whom you deploy the application. - InstallForSystem: The client installs the application only once. It's available to all users. - InstallForSystemIfResourceIsDeviceOtherwiseInstallForUser: If you deploy the application to a device, the client installs it for all users. If you deploy the application to a user, the client only installs it for that user.

parameters.name: InstallCommand
parameters.description: Specify the installation program command line to install this application.

parameters.name: InstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the InstallCommand.

parameters.name: LogonRequirementType
parameters.description: Specify the requirement for a signed-in user: - OnlyWhenNoUserLoggedOn: Only when no user is signed into Windows. - OnlyWhenUserLoggedOn: Only when a user is signed in. This option is the default. - WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn: Whether or not a user is signed in. > [!NOTE] > The value WhereOrNotUserLoggedOn is deprecated. It's replaced by WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn. If you set InstallationBehaviorType to InstallForUser, then you can't set this parameter.

parameters.name: MaximumRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the maximum allowed run time of the deployment program for this application. Set an integer value in minutes.

parameters.name: NewName
parameters.description: Specify a new name to rename this deployment type.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Add this parameter to return an object that represents the item with which you're working. By default, this cmdlet may not generate any output.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: If the application uses Windows Installer technology, specify an MSI product code to set as the detection method. When you use this parameter, it overwrites any existing detection methods.

parameters.name: RebootBehavior
parameters.description: Specify the post-installation behavior: - BasedOnExitCode: Determine behavior based on return codes. - NoAction: No specific action. - ProgramReboot: The software install program might force a device restart. - ForceReboot: Configuration Manager client will force a mandatory device restart. For more information on these behaviors, see Create applications in Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: RemoveDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses to remove.

parameters.name: RemoveLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of supported languages to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RemoveRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement rules to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RepairCommand
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command. Also configure the RepairWorkingDirectory parameter. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: RepairWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Use this parameter to configure the repair command's working directory. Also configure the RepairCommand parameter.

parameters.name: RequireUserInteraction
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to allow users to view and interact with the deployment type installation.

parameters.name: ScriptFile
parameters.description: Specify the script file to use to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter.

parameters.name: ScriptLanguage
parameters.description: If you use the ScriptFile or ScriptText parameters, use this parameter to specify the script language.

parameters.name: ScriptText
parameters.description: Specify the text of a script to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter. For more information, see About custom script detection methods.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkDeploymentMode
parameters.description: When a client uses a distribution point from a neighbor boundary group or the default site boundary group, specify the deployment option: - DoNothing: Don't download content - Download: Download content from the distribution point and run locally

parameters.name: SourceUpdateProductCode
parameters.description: If the application uses Windows Installer technology, specify an MSI product code. This product code is a GUID format. Windows Source management enables an .MSI represented by this deployment type to automatically be updated or repaired from content source files on an available distribution point.

parameters.name: UninstallCommand
parameters.description: Specifies the command line to uninstall the application. Starting in version 2006, you can specify an empty string.

parameters.name: UninstallContentLocation
parameters.description: Specify the network path to source content to use with the UninstallCommand that's different from the ContentLocation. Use this parameter when you set UninstallOption to Different.

parameters.name: UninstallOption
parameters.description: Specify what content to use with the UninstallCommand: - SameAsInstall: The install and uninstall content are the same. This option is the default. - NoneRequired: The application doesn't need content for uninstall. - Different: The uninstall content is different from the install content. Use UninstallContentLocation to specify the network path to the content that's used to uninstall the application.

parameters.name: UninstallWorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the path to use as the working directory when the client runs the UninstallCommand.

parameters.name: UserInteractionMode
parameters.description: Specify the installation program visibility: - Normal: The deployment type runs in the normal mode based on system and program defaults. This mode is the default. - Minimized: The deployment type runs minimized on client devices. Users might see the installation activity in the notification area or taskbar. - Maximized: The deployment type runs maximized on client devices. Users see all installation activity. - Hidden: The deployment type runs hidden on client devices. Users see no installation activity.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Specify an optional description for the deployment package.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Add this parameter to force remove an expired NAP update.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: Id
parameters.description: Specify the ID of a deployment package to modify.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a deployment package object to modify. To get this object, use the Get-CMSoftwareUpdateDeploymentPackage cmdlet.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Specify the name of the deployment package to modify.

parameters.name: NewName
parameters.description: Specify a new name for the deployment package.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Add this parameter to return an object that represents the item with which you're working. By default, this cmdlet may not generate any output.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Specify a package source path for the deployment package.

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: Specify the order in which the site sends the content to other sites and the distribution points in this site. The site sends high priority content before packages with medium or low priority. Packages with equal priority are sent in the order in which they're created.

parameters.name: RefreshDistributionPoint
parameters.description: Add this parameter to refresh the package on distribution points.

parameters.name: RemoveExpired
parameters.description: Add this parameter to decline updates that aren't approved and have been expired by Microsoft.

parameters.name: RemoveSuperseded
parameters.description: Add this parameter to decline updates that haven't been approved for 30 days or more, aren't currently needed by any clients, and are superseded by an approved update.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

parameters.description: Specify one of the following values for where the task sequence saves the package: - TaskSequenceWorkingFolder: Use the task sequence working directory, which is also referred to as the task sequence cache. - ClientCache: Use the Configuration Manager client cache. parameters.name: AddCondition
parameters.description: Specify a condition object to add to this step. To get this object, use one of the task sequence condition cmdlets. For example, Get-CMTSStepConditionVariable.

parameters.name: ClearCondition
parameters.description: Remove a condition from this step. Use the -Condition parameter to specify the condition to remove.

parameters.name: Condition
parameters.description: Specify a condition object to use with this step. To get this object, use one of the task sequence condition cmdlets. For example, Get-CMTSStepConditionVariable.

parameters.name: ConditionVariableName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the task sequence variable to use as a condition.

parameters.name: ConditionVariableValue
parameters.description: Specify the value of the task sequence variable to use in a condition.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Specify an optional description for this task sequence step.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: ExecutionPolicy
parameters.description: Specify the PowerShell execution policy for the scripts you allow to run on the computer. Choose one of the following policies: - AllSigned: Only run scripts signed by a trusted publisher. - Undefined: Don't define any execution policy. - Bypass: Load all configuration files and run all scripts. If you download an unsigned script from the internet, PowerShell doesn't prompt for permission before running the script.

parameters.name: FileDateTimeOperator
parameters.description: Specify a variable operator type for a file date/time condition.

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.description: Specify the path for a file condition.

parameters.name: FileTimestamp
parameters.description: Specify a date/time value to use for a file condition.

parameters.name: FileVersion
parameters.description: Specify a version string for a file condition.

parameters.name: FolderDateTimeOperator
parameters.description: Specify a variable operator for a folder date/time condition.

parameters.name: FolderPath
parameters.description: Specify the path for a folder condition.

parameters.name: FolderTimestamp
parameters.description: Specify a date/time value to use for a folder condition.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a task sequence object from which to get the Run PowerShell Script step. To get this object, use the Get-CMTaskSequence cmdlet.

parameters.name: IsAnyVersion
parameters.description: Use this parameter with the SetConditionSoftware parameter to match any version of the product.

parameters.name: IsContinueOnError
parameters.description: Use this parameter to enable the step option Continue on error. When you enable this option, if the step fails, the task sequence continues.

parameters.name: IsEnabled
parameters.description: Use this parameter to enable this task sequence step.

parameters.name: MoveToIndex
parameters.description: Move this step to the specified index position in the task sequence.

parameters.name: MsiFilePath
parameters.description: Specify the path to a Windows Installer file for a software condition.

parameters.name: Namespace
parameters.description: Specify the namespace for a WMI query condition.

parameters.name: NewStepName
parameters.description: Use this parameter to rename this task sequence step.

parameters.name: OperatorType
parameters.description: Specify an operator to use with a task sequence variable condition.

parameters.name: OutputVariableName
parameters.description: Specify the name of a custom task sequence variable. When you use this parameter, the step saves the last 1000 characters of the command output to the variable.

parameters.name: PackageId
parameters.description: Specify the package ID for the package that has the PowerShell script. The package doesn't require a program. One package can contain multiple scripts. This value is a standard package ID, for example XYZ00821. Then use the ScriptName parameter to specify the name of the script.

parameters.name: Parameter
parameters.description: Specify the parameters passed to the PowerShell script. These parameters are the same as the PowerShell script parameters on the command line. Provide parameters consumed by the script, not for the PowerShell command line. The following example contains _valid_ parameters: -MyParameter1 MyValue1 -MyParameter2 MyValue2 The following example contains _invalid_ parameters. The first two items are PowerShell command-line parameters (NoLogo and ExecutionPolicy). The script doesn't consume these parameters. -NoLogo -ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted -File MyScript.ps1 -MyParameter1 MyValue1 -MyParameter2 MyValue2 If a parameter value includes a special character or a space, use single quotation marks (') around the value. Using double quotation marks (") may cause the task sequence step to incorrectly process the parameter. For example: -Arg1 '%TSVar1%' -Arg2 '%TSVar2%' You can also set this parameter to a task sequence variable. For example, if you specify %MyScriptVariable%, when the task sequence runs the script, it adds the value of this custom variable to the PowerShell command line.

parameters.name: Query
parameters.description: Specify a WMI query string to use for a condition.

parameters.name: RegistryKey
parameters.description: Specify the key to use with a registry condition.

parameters.name: RegistryOperator
parameters.description: Specify an operator to use with a registry condition.

parameters.name: RegistryValueData
parameters.description: Specify the value data to use with a registry condition.

parameters.name: RegistryValueName
parameters.description: Specify the value name to use with a registry condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionFile
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove a file condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionFolder
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove a folder condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionIfStatement
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove an if statement condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionOperatingSystem
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove an OS condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionQueryWmi
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove a WMI query condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionRegistry
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove a registry condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionSoftware
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove a software condition.

parameters.name: RemoveConditionVariable
parameters.description: Use this parameter to remove a task sequence variable condition.

parameters.name: RootKey
parameters.description: Specify the root key to use with a registry condition.

parameters.name: ScriptName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the script to run. This script is in the package specified by the PackageId parameter.

parameters.name: SetConditionFile
parameters.description: Add a new file condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionFolder
parameters.description: Add a new folder condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionIfStatement
parameters.description: Add a new if statement condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionOperatingSystem
parameters.description: Add a new OS condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionQueryWmi
parameters.description: Add a new WMI query condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionRegistry
parameters.description: Add a new registry condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionSoftware
parameters.description: Add a new software condition.

parameters.name: SetConditionVariable
parameters.description: Add a new task sequence variable condition.

parameters.name: SourceScript
parameters.description: Instead of using the PackageId and ScriptName parameters, use this parameter to directly specify the script commands. This string value is the PowerShell commands that this step runs. You can read the contents of an existing script file into a string variable, and then use that variable for this parameter. For example: $script = [IO.File]::ReadAllText( "C:\temp\script.ps1" )

parameters.name: StatementType
parameters.description: Set the type for an if statement condition.

parameters.name: StepName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the step to select for changes.

parameters.name: StepOrder
parameters.description: Use this parameter to reorder the step in the task sequence.

parameters.name: SuccessCode
parameters.description: Specify an array of integer values as exit codes from the script that the step should evaluate as success.

parameters.name: SupportedPlatform
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the platforms for an OS condition.

parameters.name: TaskSequenceId
parameters.description: Specify the package ID of the task sequence from which to get the Run PowerShell Script step. This value is a standard package ID, for example XYZ00858.

parameters.name: TaskSequenceName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the task sequence to target for changes.

parameters.name: TimeoutMins
parameters.description: Specify an integer value that represents how long Configuration Manager allows the script to run. This value can be from 1 minute to 999 minutes. The default value is 15 minutes. If you enter a value that doesn't allow enough time for the specified script to complete successfully, this step fails. The entire task sequence could fail depending on step or group conditions. If the timeout expires, Configuration Manager terminates the PowerShell process.

parameters.name: UserName
parameters.description: Use this parameter to run the script as a Windows user account and not the local system account. Specify the name of the Windows user account. To specify the account password, use the UserPassword parameter.

parameters.name: UserPassword
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the password of the account that you specify with UserName.

parameters.name: ValueType
parameters.description: Specify the type of value for a registry condition.

parameters.name: VersionOperator
parameters.description: Specify an operator to use with a file condition.

parameters.name: WorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Specify the folder in which the command starts. This path can be up to 127 characters.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet doesn't run.

examples: Set-CMMSiDeploymentType -ApplicationName "CBI" -DeploymentTypeName "Complex install" -NewName "Advanced install" -AddLanguage "en-US","zh-CN" -Comment "New Deployment Type-updated" -EstimatedRuntimeMins 14 -LogonRequirementType OnlyWhenNoUserLoggedOn

parameters.name: AddDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses for this deployment type. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then specify those variables as an array for this parameter. For example, -AddDetectionClause $clauseFile1,$clauseFile2,$clauseFile3. You can also use Get-CMDeploymentTypeDetectionClause to get an existing detection clause from another application.

parameters.name: AddLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of language tags that the deployment type supports. For example, to add Russian (Russia), specify the tag ru-RU. For more information and a list of language tags, see Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) Reference.

parameters.name: AddRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement objects for the deployment type. To create a requirement rule object, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMRequirementRuleActiveDirectorySiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleBooleanValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCMSiteValue - New-CMRequirementRuleCommonValue - New-CMRequirementRuleDeviceOwnershipValue - New-CMRequirementRuleExistential - New-CMRequirementRuleExpression - New-CMRequirementRuleFileAttributeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFilePermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleFreeDiskSpaceValue - New-CMRequirementRuleInputTypeValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemLanguageValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOperatingSystemValue - New-CMRequirementRuleOUValue - New-CMRequirementRuleRegistryKeyPermissionValue - New-CMRequirementRuleScreenResolutionValue Starting in version 2111, you can use the Get-CMDeploymentTypeRequirement cmdlet to copy rules from another deployment type.

parameters.name: Application
parameters.description: Specify an application object for this deployment type. To get this object, use the Get-CMApplication cmdlet.

parameters.name: ApplicationId
parameters.description: Specify the ID of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the application for this deployment type.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specify an optional description for the deployment type.

parameters.name: DeploymentTypeName
parameters.description: Specify the name of the deployment type to configure.

parameters.name: DetectionClauseConnector
parameters.description: When you use the GroupDetectionClauses parameter to group detection clauses, use this parameter to specify the connector. The following example defines the OR connector: @{"LogicalName"=$clauseFile3.Setting.LogicalName;"Connector"="OR"}

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: EstimatedRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the estimated installation time, in minutes, of this deployment type for the application. Software Center displays this estimate to the user before the application installs.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Forces the command to run without asking for user confirmation.

parameters.name: ForceScriptDetection32Bit
parameters.description: If you use a custom script to detect the presence of this deployment type, set this parameter to $true to run the script as a 32-bit process on 64-bit clients.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: GroupDetectionClauses
parameters.description: When you configure rules to detect the presence of this deployment type, use this parameter to group clauses. To create a detection clause, use one of the following cmdlets: - New-CMDetectionClauseDirectory - New-CMDetectionClauseFile - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKey - New-CMDetectionClauseRegistryKeyValue - New-CMDetectionClauseWindowsInstaller Save the output of these cmdlets into a variable. Then use the following format to group clauses: $clause2.Setting.LogicalName, $clause3.Setting.LogicalName. > [!TIP] > In the Configuration Manager console, when you select the Group action, the clauses show parentheses before and after the grouped clauses.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specify a deployment type object to configure. To get this object, use the Get-CMDeploymentType cmdlet.

parameters.name: InstallationBehaviorType
parameters.description: Specify the installation behavior for this deployment type: - InstallForUser: The client only installs the application for the user to whom you deploy the application. - InstallForSystem: The client installs the application only once. It's available to all users. - InstallForSystemIfResourceIsDeviceOtherwiseInstallForUser: If you deploy the application to a device, the client installs it for all users. If you deploy the application to a user, the client only installs it for that user.

parameters.name: InstallTaskSequenceId
parameters.description: The ID of the task sequence to install the app.

parameters.name: LogonRequirementType
parameters.description: Specify the requirement for a signed-in user: - OnlyWhenNoUserLoggedOn: Only when no user is signed into Windows. - OnlyWhenUserLoggedOn: Only when a user is signed in. This option is the default. - WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn: Whether or not a user is signed in. > [!NOTE] > The value WhereOrNotUserLoggedOn is deprecated. It's replaced by WhetherOrNotUserLoggedOn. If you set InstallationBehaviorType to InstallForUser, then you can't set this parameter.

parameters.name: MaximumRuntimeMins
parameters.description: Specify the maximum allowed run time of the deployment program for this application. Set an integer value in minutes.

parameters.name: NewName
parameters.description: Specify a new name to rename this deployment type.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Add this parameter to return an object that represents the item with which you're working. By default, this cmdlet may not generate any output.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: If the application uses Windows Installer technology, specify an MSI product code to set as the detection method. When you use this parameter, it overwrites any existing detection methods.

parameters.name: RebootBehavior
parameters.description: Specify the post-installation behavior: - BasedOnExitCode: Determine behavior based on return codes. - NoAction: No specific action. - ProgramReboot: The software install program might force a device restart. - ForceReboot: Configuration Manager client will force a mandatory device restart. For more information on these behaviors, see Create applications in Configuration Manager.

parameters.name: RemoveDetectionClause
parameters.description: Specify an array of detection method clauses to remove.

parameters.name: RemoveLanguage
parameters.description: Specify an array of supported languages to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RemoveRequirement
parameters.description: Specify an array of requirement rules to remove from this deployment type.

parameters.name: RequireUserInteraction
parameters.description: Set this parameter to $true to allow users to view and interact with the deployment type installation.

parameters.name: ScriptFile
parameters.description: Specify the script file to use to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter.

parameters.name: ScriptLanguage
parameters.description: If you use the ScriptFile or ScriptText parameters, use this parameter to specify the script language.

parameters.name: ScriptText
parameters.description: Specify the text of a script to detect this deployment type. Also use the ScriptLanguage parameter. For more information, see About custom script detection methods.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkDeploymentMode
parameters.description: When a client uses a distribution point from a neighbor boundary group or the default site boundary group, specify the deployment option: - DoNothing: Don't download content - Download: Download content from the distribution point and run locally

parameters.name: UninstallTaskSequenceId
parameters.description: The ID of the task sequence to uninstall the app.

parameters.name: UserInteractionMode
parameters.description: Specify the installation program visibility: - Normal: The deployment type runs in the normal mode based on system and program defaults. This mode is the default. - Minimized: The deployment type runs minimized on client devices. Users might see the installation activity in the notification area or taskbar. - Maximized: The deployment type runs maximized on client devices. Users see all installation activity. - Hidden: The deployment type runs hidden on client devices. Users see no installation activity.

parameters.name: AllowSharedContent
parameters.description: Indicates whether clients use shared content. If this value is $True, clients attempt to download content from other clients that downloaded that content. If this value is $False, clients do not attempt to download from other clients.

parameters.name: CollectionName
parameters.description: Specifies the ID of a device or user collection.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Specifies a comment for the deployment.

parameters.name: DeploymentAvailableDateTime
parameters.description: Specifies, as a DateTime object, the date and time that the deployment becomes available. To obtain a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeploymentAvailableDay
parameters.description: Obsolete. Use *DeploymentAvailableDateTime*.

parameters.name: DeploymentAvailableTime
parameters.description: Obsolete. Use *DeploymentAvailableDateTime* instead.

parameters.name: DeploymentExpireDateTime
parameters.description: Specifies, as a DateTime object, the date and time that the deployment expires. To obtain a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeploymentExpireDay
parameters.description: Obsolete. Use *DeploymentExpireDateTime* instead.

parameters.name: DeploymentExpireTime
parameters.description: Obsolete. Use *DeploymentExpireDateTime*.

parameters.name: DeploymentStartDateTime
parameters.description: Specifies, as a DateTime object, the date and time that the deployment starts. To obtain a DateTime object, use the Get-Date cmdlet.

parameters.name: DeploymentStartDay
parameters.description: Obsolete. Use *DeploymentStartDateTime*.

parameters.name: DeploymentStartTime
parameters.description: Obsolete. Use *DeploymentStartDateTime*.

parameters.name: DeployPurpose
parameters.description: Specifies the purpose for the deployment. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - Available - Required

parameters.name: DeviceProgram
parameters.description: Specifies a device program.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: FastNetworkOption
parameters.description: Specifies client behavior on a fast network. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - DownloadContentFromDistributionPointAndRunLocally - RunProgramFromDistributionPoint

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: Package
parameters.description: Specifies a package object. To obtain a package object, use the Get-CMPackage cmdlet.

parameters.name: PackageId
parameters.description: Specifies the ID of a package.

parameters.name: PackageName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of a package.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Returns the current working object. By default, this cmdlet does not generate any output.

parameters.name: PersistOnWriteFilterDevice
parameters.description: Indicates whether to enable write filters for embedded devices. For a value of $True, the device commits changes during a maintenance window. This action requires a restart. For a value of $False, the device saves changes in an overlay and commits them later.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: Specifies a program.

parameters.name: ProgramName
parameters.description: Specifies the name of a program.

parameters.name: RecurUnit
parameters.description: Specifies a unit for a recurring deployment. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - Days - Hours - Minutes

parameters.name: RecurValue
parameters.description: Specifies how often a deployment recurs. This parameter depends on the unit type specified in the *RecurUnit* parameter. This value can be between 1 and 23 if the unit is Hours, between 1 and 31 if the unit is Days, or between 1 and 59 if the unit is Minutes.

parameters.name: Rerun
parameters.description: Indicates whether the deployment reruns. If this value is $True, the deployment runs again for clients as specified in the *RerunBehavior* parameter. If this value is $False, the deployment does not run again.

parameters.name: RerunBehavior
parameters.description: Specifies how a deployment reruns on a client. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - AlwaysRerunProgram. Rerun as scheduled, even if the deployment succeeded. You can use this value for recurring deployments. - NeverRerunDeployedProgram. Does not rerun, even if the deployment failed or files changed. - RerunIfFailedPreviousAttempt. Rerun, as scheduled, if the deployment failed on the previous attempt. - RerunIfSucceededOnpreviousAttempt. Rerun only if the previous attempt succeeded. You can use this value for updates that depend on the previous update.

parameters.name: RunFromSoftwareCenter
parameters.description: Indicates whether to run from Software Center.

parameters.name: Schedule
parameters.description: Specifies a schedule object for the deployment.

parameters.name: ScheduleEvent
parameters.description: Specifies an array of schedule event types. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - AsSoonAsPossible - LogOff - LogOn - SendWakeUpPacket

parameters.name: SendWakeupPacket
parameters.description: Indicates whether to send a wake up packet to computers before the deployment begins. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager wakes a computer from sleep. If this value is $False, it does not wake computers from sleep. For computers to wake, you must first configure Wake On LAN.

parameters.name: SlowNetworkOption
parameters.description: Specifies how Configuration Manager deploys this package in a slow network. The acceptable values for this parameter are: - DoNotRunProgram - DownloadContentFromDistributionPointAndLocally - RunProgramFromDistributionPoint

parameters.name: SoftwareInstallation
parameters.description: Indicates whether to install the deployed software outside of maintenance windows. A maintenance window is a specified period of time used for computer maintenance and updates. If this value is $True, the Configuration Manager installs software according to schedule, even if the schedule falls outside a maintenance window. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager does not install deployed software outside any windows, but waits for a maintenance window.

parameters.name: StandardProgram
parameters.description: Indicates that the program type in the deployment package is standard program.

parameters.name: SystemRestart
parameters.description: Indicates whether a system restarts outside a maintenance window. A maintenance window is a specified period of time used for computer maintenance and updates. If this value is $True, any required restart takes place without regard to maintenance windows. If this value is $False, the computer does not restart outside a maintenance window.

parameters.name: UseMeteredNetwork
parameters.description: Indicates whether to allow clients to download content over a metered Internet connection after the deadline, which may incur additional expense.

parameters.name: UseUtc
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), also known as Greenwich Mean Time. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager uses UTC for this deployment. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager uses local time.

parameters.name: UseUtcForAvailableSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use UTC for available schedule. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager uses UTC. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager uses local time.

parameters.name: UseUtcForExpireSchedule
parameters.description: Indicates whether to use UTC for expire schedule. If this value is $True, Configuration Manager uses UTC. If this value is $False, Configuration Manager uses local time.

parameters.name: Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

parameters.name: DisableWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter treats wildcard characters as literal character values. You can't combine it with ForceWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: ForceWildcardHandling
parameters.description: This parameter processes wildcard characters and may lead to unexpected behavior (not recommended). You can't combine it with DisableWildcardHandling.

parameters.name: Id
parameters.description: Specifies the CI_ID and ModelID properties (the same value) of an application.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: Specifies an application object. To obtain an application object, use the Get-CMApplication cmdlet.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Specifies the name of the application.
